customer.commercial_context: Opportunity for phased automation plan in corrugated plant conversion and intralogistics.

summary: Sigmaq is not rejecting the opportunity. The response from Rafael indicates a staged buying pattern: focus first on waste handling and trim flow; wait to evaluate bobbin logistics and palletization in separate session and budget windows. The opportunity should be managed as a modular roadmap rather than a single full-plant request.
source_signals: Email from Rafael indicates agreement to a first technical session.
Explicit prioritization of waste handling and trim flow in the first phase.
Deferred bobbin logistics and palletization to second/third sessions with separate budget.
Customer asks to validate layouts and technical fit before expansion.

strategic_interpretation.main_point: This is a phased conversion sale, not a rejection.
strategic_interpretation.reality: Rafael is signaling interest in a first ROI-focused technical win and is not yet ready to commit to the broader automation roadmap under a single scope.
strategic_interpretation.commercial_implication: The correct strategy is to win the first phase, prove layout and performance, then use that success as a bridge to the next automation modules.
strategic_interpretation.risk_if_we_push_too_far: If we push the full vision in one project, we risk losing the sale because the budget is fragmented across phases and the customer wants risk reduction first.

decision_log.decision: Customer accepts technical session structure, but scoped to first phase only.
decision_log.details: They propose focusing on line waste handling and trim flow for corrugator-to-embaladora processes.

decision_log.decision: Bobbin logistics / paper reel handling and palletization are deferred to later stages.
decision_log.details: This indicates separate budget and a differentiated technical discussion path.

decision_log.decision: Target phase 1 as the commercial entry point.
decision_log.details: This is the most probable win path because it addresses a highly visible bottleneck with clear operational value.

phases.name: Waste handling and trim flow
phases.objective: Solve the most visible operational pain point and secure a visible ROI case.
phases.value_proposition: Reduction in waste, better trim flow, more stable process between corrugator and embaladora, limited technical risk and faster decision cycle.
phases.recommended_positioning: Fase de entrada, de demostración técnica y retorno medible.

phases.name: Bobbin logistics and paper reel feed to corrugator
phases.objective: Expand automation to upstream material flow once phase 1 is validated.
phases.value_proposition: Better logistics flow, reduction in manual intervention, overall plant throughput stabilization.
phases.recommended_positioning: Second session with separate budget and technical scope.

phases.name: Automatic palletization, WIP, and AMR integration
phases.objective: Broaden the solution after the customer sees first-phase success and budget availability increases.
phases.value_proposition: Higher efficiency, lower labor dependency, scalability and future-proof intralogistics.
phases.recommended_positioning: Roadmap item, not immediate proposal scope.

commercial_focus: Waste handling and trim management as phase 1 entry point.
Layout review with Sigmaq around current operational constraints.
Technical validation for flow continuity and material handling efficiency.
ROI proof through concrete bottleneck reduction and process reliability.
Use phase 1 to unlock the next budget windows for bobbin logistics and palletization.
recommended_actions: Send a direct technical response acknowledging phase prioritization and proposing a dedicated session for phase 1.
Prepare a layout-focused technical pack around waste/trim flow and machine interfaces.
Clarify what is excluded vs included in phase 1 to avoid scope confusion.
Frame bobbin logistics and palletization as sequential follow-up scopes with independent business cases.
Document the commercial rationale and keep a decision log in the repository for continuity.
signals_of_opportunity: The scope is being broken into manageable business units.
Budget signal is not negative; it is staged.
risks: Pushing outbound full-plant automation too early may reduce win probability.
Scope drift if the first meeting mixes phase 1 and phase 2 topics in the same discussion.
Failure to document the sequence may allow the customer to lose focus and delay the sale.
Lack of clear commercial packaging around phase 1 may make the project look too small or too technical.
next_milestone: Define the first meeting around waste/trim scope, evidence, layout review, and required technical inputs from Sigmaq.
